medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The Center for Student Well-being promotes and fosters student growth through leadership, engagement and wellness programs.
https://www.geisinger.edu/gchs/education/departments/student-life/student-wellness
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Student may request a leave of absence (LOA) by working with the Associate Dean of Admissions and Student Affairs. LOA status can be granted for a minimum of one month and maximum of one year. Students who do not return to full-time status at the end of the leave and who have not reapplied for renewal of the leave are considered to have withdrawn from TCMC and need to reapply through the Associate Deans of Academic Affairs and Student Affairs if they wish to return at some future date.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine recognizes the contributions of student clubs and organizations that enhance the quality of student life and the college community. Clubs and organizations offer students the opportunity to participate in academic, cultural, social and athletic activities consistent with the development of knowledge, skills, values and attitudes expected from healthcare professionals. Numerous standing clubs exist; however, the Office of Student Affairs is always interested in meeting student needs and works collaboratively with the Medical Student Council, the governing board, to welcome suggestions for starting new clubs.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Medical Science Building (MSB) is home to Geisinger College of Health Science's academic programs. Opened in April 2011 and dedicated in October 2011, the 185,000-square-foot MSB occupies a three-acre parcel of land in downtown Scranton, PA. The space includes a Clinical Skills and Simulation Center, Gross Anatomy Laboratory, our 95% digital library, lounge and study space, and educational space. This building in downtown Scranton is easily accessible to all Scranton hospitals.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students have access to a variety of housing options on the North campus (Scranton) for phase 1 and on the clinical campuses for phases 2 and 3.  Housing is not provided by Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine.

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The learning environment at Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine cultivates a supportive environment and minimizes competition among students. Faculty and staff are attentive to students' needs and will work together to ensure success.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
Students are responsible for arranging and funding their own transportation to and from all assigned clinical sites, including those located off-campus or outside the immediate vicinity of 
the Medical Sciences Building (Scranton) This includes travel for required clerkships, electives, intern or externships, and other clinical learning experiences.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine has an integrated advising system, coordinated through the Office of Student Affairs, which leverages faculty and staff as advisors.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: The Phase 2 curriculum provides comparable, high-quality, foundational clinical experiences through inpatient and ambulatory block rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The Phase 1 curriculum encompasses foundational education rooted in basic, clinical and health system sciences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The advanced clinical experience phase is time for learners to complete their core curriculum requirements and explore their own interests in medicine through sub-internships and electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Students are required to submit specified documentation prior to matriculation including, but not limited to: final transcripts, background checks, drug screening, and health documents.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine does not compute a class rank or do an overall rating system.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: All courses use active learning educational experiences instead of lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Total Health Curriculum is built on the science of learning and uses an evidence-based approach to train skilled, compassionate physicians who provide individualized care of patients and promote health in the communities they serve. In addition to providing a fully integrated and immersive educational experience in basic, clinical and health systems sciences, the curriculum emphasizes six themes, including Social Justice and Health Equity, Health System Citizenship, Primary Care, Personal and Professional Development, Community Immersion and Population Health. These themes will guide the training of physicians who are resilient, collaborative and ready to assume leadership roles in evolving healthcare settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: While primary care is fundamental to the mission of the institution, students have matriculated and gone on to residency programs in all specialties.  Geisinger believes in primary care and its power to evolve medicine from disease management to enabling stronger, healthier, more vibrant communities.  The Abigail Geisinger Scholars Program was designed to allow students to pursue their primary care goals without the worry of student loan debt. For more information, visit: https://www.geisinger.edu/gchs/education/departments/division-enrollment-management/financial-aid/md-program/abigail-geisinger-scholars-program
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Our biomedical research and training programs target the health issues that are prevalent in northeastern, central, and northcentral Pennsylvania, including the cancers that exhibit a high incidence in the region, chronic disease associated with aging, and significant needs in primary care, mental health, and community medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText:
Phase 1 – Principles of Medical Science and Practice
Phase 2 – Core Clinical Immersion
Phase 3 – Career Differentiation and Exploration
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The Summer Research Immersion Program (SRIP) is an eight-week program open to first-year medical students at Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine who are in good academic standing.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine is unique among academic health centers. The School of Medicine offers a community-based model of undergraduate medical education with regional campuses in Danville, Lewistown, Sayre, and the Northeast (Scranton and Wilkes-Barre). The School’s innovative Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree curriculum, focused on caring for people in the context of their lives and their community, attracts the next generation of physicians and scientists from within its region, as well as from across Pennsylvania and the nation.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Geisinger Commonwealth School of Medicine will educate aspiring physicians and scientists to serve society using a community-based, patient-centered, interprofessional and evidence-based model of education that is committed fairness and respect for all, promotes discovery and utilizes innovative techniques.

medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
The admissions interview is a critical piece of the application process. It provides the Admissions Committee with deeper insight into who you are as a candidate. Also, it gives the candidate a more in-depth look at the School of Medicine's Total Health Curriculum, which is built on the science of learning and uses an evidence-based approach to train skilled, compassionate physicians who provide individualized care of patients and promote health in their communities.

After the Admissions Committee reviews the applications, selected applicants will receive an email invitation to interview at the School of Medicine. The Committee will consider the candidates' academic potential for success and alignment with the school's mission and values.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
To further our core mission of adding physicians to critically underserved areas of healthcare, we established an integrated 6-year Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMS)/Medical Doctorate (MD) parallel curriculum program.

This new program builds on the strengths of Geisinger’s MD program and OMS residency program. In our new combined OMS-MD program, you’ll gain a deeper foundational knowledge of medicine, integrated with your subspecialty training in oral and maxillofacial surgery.

The Abigail Geisinger Scholars Program was created to address the rising debt of medical students and to repopulate the physician shortage in Geisinger’s primary service areas within Pennsylvania. Geisinger wants its smart, hardworking medical students to be free to practice medicine the way every future doctor imagines it — through meaningful, long-term relationships with people who become more like family.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Abigail Geisinger Scholars accepted into the Primary Care 3+3 Accelerated Program complete medical school in three years, followed by a three-year residency- with a pathway to match in one of Geisinger's residency programs for internal medicine or family medicine.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants accepted to the School of Medicine and subsequently accepted to the Abigail Geisinger Scholars program.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Applicants who indicate their interest in the Abigail Geisinger Scholars Program and are accepted for admission to the School of Medicine will be invited to interview for the Scholars Program.  If accepted into the Abigail Geisinger Scholars Program, applicants will be invited to apply for and complete the interview process for the 3+3 program.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: In addition to meeting all application deadlines and completing all required interviews, all applicants must be either US Citizens for Permanent Residents.
